lines.text: Flight 1549 leaves LaGuardia for Charlotte, with a hundred and fifty five people on board.
Captain Chesley Sullenberger and First Officer Jeffrey Skiles climb out over the Bronx.
About two minutes after takeoff, at twenty eight hundred feet, a flock of Canada geese.
Birds hit both engines. Both lose thrust, almost at once.
Mayday, mayday, mayday. Hit birds. We've lost thrust in both engines. We're turning back towards LaGuardia.
The captain starts the APU, and takes the controls.
Air traffic control offers a return to LaGuardia.
We're unable. We may end up in the Hudson.
We can't do it. We're gonna be in the Hudson.
This is the captain. Brace for impact.
The flight attendants shout their commands. Brace, brace. Heads down, stay down.
Wings level. Nose up. Two hundred and eight seconds after the strike.
Everyone climbs out, onto the wings and into the rafts. The water is five degrees.
Every one of the one hundred and fifty five people on board survived.
They called it the Miracle on the Hudson.
